description: Only standing orders with an amount strictly greater than 2802 are used in the per-purpose averages and in the overall average.

d.request: For each `order.k_symbol`, including the blank code as its own group, average `order.amount` over standing orders with `amount > 2802`; then take the unweighted average of those per-purpose averages and list each purpose whose average exceeds it, with its `k_symbol`, unrounded average amount, and unrounded difference from the overall average.
d.sql: WITH purpose_averages AS (SELECT k_symbol, AVG(amount) AS average_amount FROM `order` WHERE amount > 2802 GROUP BY k_symbol), overall_average AS (SELECT AVG(average_amount) AS average_amount FROM purpose_averages) SELECT p.k_symbol, p.average_amount, p.average_amount - o.average_amount AS difference FROM purpose_averages AS p CROSS JOIN overall_average AS o WHERE p.average_amount > o.average_amount

b.request: For each `order.k_symbol`, including the blank code as its own group, average `order.amount` over orders with `amount > 2802`; then take the unweighted average of those group averages and return each code whose average exceeds it, with its group average and the unrounded difference.
b.sql: WITH group_averages AS (SELECT k_symbol, AVG(amount) AS group_average FROM "order" WHERE amount > 2802 GROUP BY k_symbol), overall AS (SELECT AVG(group_average) AS unweighted_average FROM group_averages) SELECT g.k_symbol, g.group_average, g.group_average - o.unweighted_average AS difference FROM group_averages AS g CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE g.group_average > o.unweighted_average
b.raw: For each `order.k_symbol`, including the blank code as its own group, average `order.amount` over orders with `amount > 2802`; then take the unweighted average of those group averages and return each code whose average exceeds it, with its group average and the unrounded difference.

c.request: Using an `amount` of 2802 as the cutoff for a large standing order (the `order` table), compute the average `amount` of the large orders for each payment purpose code (`k_symbol`), treating the blank purpose code as a group of its own. Then take the simple average of those per-purpose averages. Which purposes have an average above that overall figure? For each, list the `k_symbol`, its average amount, and how far it exceeds the overall figure (purpose average minus overall figure), without rounding. Only standing orders with an amount strictly greater than 2802 are used in the per-purpose averages and in the overall average.
c.sql: WITH purpose_averages AS (SELECT k_symbol, AVG(amount) AS average_amount FROM "order" WHERE amount > 2802 GROUP BY k_symbol), overall_average AS (SELECT AVG(average_amount) AS overall_amount FROM purpose_averages) SELECT p.k_symbol, p.average_amount, p.average_amount - o.overall_amount AS amount_above_overall FROM purpose_averages AS p CROSS JOIN overall_average AS o WHERE p.average_amount > o.overall_amount

a.request: Considering only standing orders (the `order` table) whose `amount` is greater than 2802, compute the average `amount` for each payment purpose code (`k_symbol`), treating the blank purpose code as a group of its own. Then take the simple average of those per-purpose averages. Which purposes have an average above that overall figure? For each, list the `k_symbol`, its average amount, and how far it exceeds the overall figure (purpose average minus overall figure), without rounding.
a.sql: WITH purpose_averages AS (SELECT k_symbol, AVG(amount) AS average_amount FROM `order` WHERE amount > 2802 GROUP BY k_symbol), overall AS (SELECT AVG(average_amount) AS overall_average FROM purpose_averages) SELECT p.k_symbol, p.average_amount, p.average_amount - o.overall_average AS amount_above_overall FROM purpose_averages AS p CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE p.average_amount > o.overall_average
